name: Bain & Company
seo_title: Bain interview process: what to expect
description: What Bain & Company's own careers pages say about applying for consulting roles: the digital assessment, case interviews and how to prepare.
intro: This guide sums up what Bain & Company's own careers pages say about applying for a consulting role, from the digital assessment to case and experience interviews. It reflects those pages as we checked them on 15 October 2026. Bain says the steps can vary by role and office, so check its careers site before you apply.

items.text: Bain says each role has its own process, but for most roles your application is reviewed, you may have a call with a recruiter, and you then have several rounds of interviews.
For consulting roles, Bain says the process typically has two parts: a digital assessment first, then one or more case interviews.
Bain suggests that students contact an on-campus recruiter to find out when to apply for internships and other roles.
Bain says you will learn how each interview went afterwards, and that any feedback is based on an objective scoring system.
Bain warns of job scams and says it never interviews over instant messaging, and never asks candidates to buy products or services or to process payments on its behalf.
Candidates for intern and full-time consulting roles may be asked to take a digital assessment, depending on the role and the office.
If an assessment is required, it is a compulsory step, and Bain will not consider an application if the assessment is not finished by the deadline.
If an assessment is required, Bain emails you after you apply to say whether it is Sova or Test Gorilla, and the deadline for finishing it is also sent by email.
The assessment takes about 30 to 40 minutes.
Bain says the assessment reflects skills needed in consulting, such as problem solving, communication and analysis, and that it is one part of the review of your application.
Pen, paper and a calculator are allowed in the assessment, but Bain says calculators are not allowed in the interviews that follow.
You must take the assessment on your own. AI tools are strictly prohibited, and Bain says this includes recording, screenshots and any software that transcribes or gives feedback.

Bain says no preparation is needed for Test Gorilla, which should be done in one sitting; for Sova, it points to sample questions on Sova's own preparation pages, and the sections can be spread out as long as all are done by the deadline.
Bain says timings vary by role and office, but applicants can expect to hear back within 60 days of taking the assessment.
Bain describes a case interview as a structured conversation in which you work through a real business problem, and says case interviews are used for consulting roles only.
Bain says it is not looking for one right answer but for how you think, how you structure problems and how you build on ideas as the conversation moves on.
Bain's interviewing page says these interviews reward precision as well as creativity, and that Bain provides all the materials you need.
Bain's practice cases suggest taking a minute or two to plan your approach, walking the interviewer through your structure, and then proposing where you would like to start.
For in-person interviews, Bain suggests bringing pen and paper for notes and case work; for virtual interviews, it suggests telling the interviewer when you are taking notes.
Bain describes one interview type as a conversation with future colleagues about your past experience, whether personal, academic or otherwise.
Bain says to come ready to talk about its operating principles and to connect your skills and expertise to the role.
Some roles include at least one behavioural interview, while others add behavioural questions about how you handled past work, academic or personal challenges.
Whatever the role, Bain says it looks for people who can explain why they want to join Bain in particular.
Bain says every candidate for a given role is asked the same questions, to reduce bias.
Bain's case interview page has two practice cases written by Bain, called Coffee Shop Co. and FashionCo.
The same page lists interview tips, such as clarifying the objective, structuring your thinking, thinking aloud and asking thoughtful questions.
It also links to free preparation material and sample cases from other companies that Bain has found helpful.
Bain suggests knowing your CV well, finding out about your interviewers, reading Bain's operating principles and writing your own questions in advance.
Bain says it will never ask you to memorise and recite material, because it is more interested in how you think.

practice_advice: Practise saying your structure out loud before you start any analysis, so the interviewer can follow your plan.
Do short, timed mental maths drills most days. Mock Partner's drills cover mental maths, chart reading and market sizing.
Run full practice cases from the opening question to a final recommendation, and finish each one with a summary of a minute or less.
Prepare two or three stories from your own experience, each with a clear situation, what you did and the result, and practise telling each in about two minutes.
After every practice case, write down one thing to improve and focus on it in the next one.
